#Created with AI, used in the next 4 visualizations
#import CSV files
df_2020 = pd.read_csv("2020.csv")
df_2021 = pd.read_csv("2021.csv")
df_2022 = pd.read_csv("2022.csv")
df_2023 = pd.read_csv("2023.csv")
df_2024 = pd.read_csv("2024.csv")

national2020 = df_2020.loc[1873]
national2021 = df_2021.loc[2045]
national2022 = df_2022.loc[2236]
national2023 = df_2023.loc[2320]
national2024 = df_2024.loc[2402]

#Combine the frames
national_data_list = [
    national2020.to_frame().T,
    national2021.to_frame().T,
    national2022.to_frame().T,
    national2023.to_frame().T,
    national2024.to_frame().T
]
combined_national_df = pd.concat(national_data_list, ignore_index=True)

# --- New code to prepare state-level data ---
df_list = [df_2020, df_2021, df_2022, df_2023, df_2024]
combined_state_df = pd.concat(df_list, ignore_index=True)

# Filter for state-level data (agglvl_code = 56 for state, own_code = 5 for private)
# and ensure we are not including national aggregates 'US000'
#Used for maps
state_level_df = combined_state_df[
    (combined_state_df['agglvl_code'] == 56) &
    (combined_state_df['own_code'] == 5) &
    (combined_state_df['area_fips'] != 'US000')
].copy()

state_level_df['id'] = state_level_df['area_fips'].astype(str).str[:2].astype(int)

df = pd.read_csv('ai_job_replacement_2020_2026_v2.csv')

df_grouped = df.groupby(['job_role', 'industry']).agg(
    Average_Salary=('salary_before_usd', 'mean'),
    AI_Risk_Score=('automation_risk_percent', 'mean'),
    Employment_Size=('job_id', 'count')
).reset_index()

bins = [-1, 33, 66, 101]
labels = ['Low Risk', 'Medium Risk', 'High Risk']
df_grouped['Risk_Category'] = pd.cut(df_grouped['AI_Risk_Score'], bins=bins, labels=labels)

sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

color_palette = {'Low Risk': '#2ecc71', 'Medium Risk': '#f1c40f', 'High Risk': '#e74c3c'}

ax = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Average_Salary',
    y='AI_Risk_Score',
    hue='Risk_Category',
    size='Employment_Size',
    sizes=(20, 500),
    palette=color_palette,
    alpha=0.7,
    edgecolor='black'
)

sns.regplot(
    data=df,
    x='Average_Salary',
    y='AI_Risk_Score',
    scatter=False,
    color='darkgray',
    line_kws={'linestyle': '--', 'linewidth': 2}
)

plt.title('Vulnerability to AI Automation by Average Job Salary', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Average Salary (USD)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
plt.ylabel('AI Automation Risk Score (0-100)', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

ax.set_xscale('log')

formatter = FuncFormatter(lambda x, pos: f'${x:,.0f}')
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)

plt.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', frameon=True)

plt.tight_layout()

plt.show()

)

sector_order = (
    df_industry_compare[df_industry_compare["year"] == "2025"]
    .sort_values("adoption_pct", ascending=False)["sector"].tolist()
)

# Pre-processing data
df_high = merged_df.nlargest(10, "Probability").rename(columns={"OCC_TITLE": "occupation", "A_MEDIAN": "salary", "Probability": "risk"}).reset_index(drop=True)
df_low  = merged_df.nsmallest(10, "Probability").rename(columns={"OCC_TITLE": "occupation", "A_MEDIAN": "salary", "Probability": "risk"}).reset_index(drop=True)

HIGH_TITLES = {0:"Telemarketers",1:"Travel Agents",2:"Title Examiners",3:"Insurance Underwriters",4:"Bookkeeping Clerks",5:"Tellers",6:"Packers",7:"Tax Preparers",8:"Cargo & Freight Agents",9:"Cashiers"}
LOW_TITLES  = {0:"Speech Pathologists",1:"Occupational Therapists",2:"Family Practitioners",3:"Psychiatrists",4:"IT Managers",5:"Engineering Managers",6:"Dentists",7:"Pharmacists",8:"Elementary Teachers",9:"Postsecondary Teachers"}

df_high["occupation"] = df_high.index.map(lambda i: HIGH_TITLES.get(i, df_high.loc[i, "occupation"]))
df_low["occupation"]  = df_low.index.map(lambda i: LOW_TITLES.get(i, df_low.loc[i, "occupation"]))
df_high["label"] = df_high["risk"].map(lambda x: f"{x:.0%}")
df_low["label"]  = df_low["risk"].map(lambda x: f"{x:.2%}")

low_max = df_low["risk"].max()

raw = pd.read_csv(
    "4_Investment_By_Country.csv",
    skiprows=2,
    usecols=["Country / Region", "2019 ($B)", "2020 ($B)", "2021 ($B)", "2022 ($B)", "2023 ($B)", "2024 ($B)"],
)

raw = raw[raw["Country / Region"].isin(["United States", "China", "European Union"])]

investment_data = raw.melt(
    id_vars="Country / Region",
    value_vars=["2019 ($B)", "2020 ($B)", "2021 ($B)", "2022 ($B)", "2023 ($B)", "2024 ($B)"],
    var_name="year",

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

print("Loading...")

try:
    df_ecec = pd.read_excel('ecec-civilian-dataset.xlsx', sheet_name='Civilian dataset')
except ValueError:
    df_ecec = pd.read_excel('ecec-civilian-dataset.xlsx', sheet_name=1)

df_ecec = df_ecec[(df_ecec['Year'] == 2025) & (df_ecec['Period'] == 'September')]
df_ecec = df_ecec[df_ecec['Datatype'] == 'Cost of compensation (Cost per hour worked)']

df_ecec = df_ecec[df_ecec['Compensation component'].isin(['Total compensation', 'Wages and salaries'])]

df_ecec['Estimate'] = pd.to_numeric(df_ecec['Estimate'], errors='coerce')

df_pivot = df_ecec.pivot_table(
    index='Occupation',
    columns='Compensation component',
    values='Estimate',
    aggfunc='mean'
).reset_index()

df_pivot['Benefit_Multiplier'] = df_pivot['Total compensation'] / df_pivot['Wages and salaries']

df_cps = pd.read_excel('cpsa2024.xlsx', sheet_name='cpsaat39', skiprows=5)

df_cps.columns = [
    'Occupation_Raw',
    'Total_Workers', 'Total_Median_Weekly',
    'Men_Workers', 'Men_Median_Weekly',
    'Women_Workers', 'Women_Median_Weekly'
]
df_cps = df_cps.dropna(subset=['Occupation_Raw'])

for col in ['Men_Median_Weekly', 'Women_Median_Weekly']:
    df_cps[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_cps[col], errors='coerce')

df_cps['Men_Base_Salary'] = df_cps['Men_Median_Weekly'] * 52
df_cps['Women_Base_Salary'] = df_cps['Women_Median_Weekly'] * 52

name_mapping = {
    'Management, professional, and related occupations': 'Management, professional and related occupations',
    'Management, business, and financial operations occupations': 'Management, business, and financial occupations',
    'Service occupations': 'Service occupations',
    'Sales and office occupations': 'Sales and office occupations',
    'Natural resources, construction, and maintenance occupations': 'Natural resources, construction, and maintenance occupations',
    'Production, transportation, and material moving occupations': 'Production, transportation, and material moving occupations'
}
df_cps['Occupation_Clean'] = df_cps['Occupation_Raw'].map(name_mapping).fillna(df_cps['Occupation_Raw'])

df_story = pd.merge(
    df_cps,
    df_pivot[['Occupation', 'Benefit_Multiplier']],
    left_on='Occupation_Clean',
    right_on='Occupation',
    how='inner'
)

df_story['Men_Total_Comp'] = df_story['Men_Base_Salary'] * df_story['Benefit_Multiplier']
df_story['Women_Total_Comp'] = df_story['Women_Base_Salary'] * df_story['Benefit_Multiplier']

print("\n--- Success! Here is your perfectly merged data ---")
print(df_story[['Occupation_Clean', 'Men_Base_Salary', 'Men_Total_Comp', 'Women_Base_Salary', 'Women_Total_Comp']].head())

import altair as alt
import pandas as pd

high_benefit = [
    'Management, professional and related occupations',
    'Management, business, and financial occupations'
]
low_benefit = [
    'Service occupations',
    'Sales and office occupations'
]

df_filtered = df_story[df_story['Occupation_Clean'].isin(high_benefit + low_benefit)].copy()

df_filtered['Broad_Tier'] = df_filtered['Occupation_Clean'].apply(
    lambda x: 'High-Benefit Roles' if x in high_benefit else 'Low-Benefit Roles'
)

df_men = df_filtered.groupby('Broad_Tier')['Men_Workers'].sum().reset_index()
df_men['Gender'] = 'Men'
df_men.rename(columns={'Men_Workers': 'Workers'}, inplace=True)

df_women = df_filtered.groupby('Broad_Tier')['Women_Workers'].sum().reset_index()
df_women['Gender'] = 'Women'
df_women.rename(columns={'Women_Workers': 'Workers'}, inplace=True)

df_simple = pd.concat([df_men, df_women])

bars = alt.Chart(df_simple).mark_bar(size=80).encode(

### Data Cleaning for NCSG Data Unemployment

import pandas as pd

# IMPORTANT
# Need to change the input file, output file, and YEAR variables below for every new file
# All input files for this dataset usually start with 'ecpg{year}'. For the sake of convention, our output file will be named 'cs_related_employment_{year},csv'
INPUT_FILE = "epcg23.csv"
OUTPUT_FILE = "cs_related_employment_2023.csv"
YEAR = 2023


CS_AND_RELATED_CODES = [116710, 116730, 116740, 116760, 116770]

print(f"Loading NSCG {YEAR} data...")
df = pd.read_csv(INPUT_FILE)


# IMPORTANT: Switch 'N2BAMED' with 'NBAMED' for dataset 2017 or older.
mask = df['N2BAMED'].isin(CS_AND_RELATED_CODES)
cs_df = df[mask].copy()

print(f"Found {len(cs_df)} sampled individuals with CS-related first bachelor's degree.")
print("Computing weighted estimates...\n")


weight_employed = cs_df[cs_df['LFSTAT'] == 1]['WTSURVY'].sum()
weight_unemployed = cs_df[cs_df['LFSTAT'] == 2]['WTSURVY'].sum()
weight_not_in_labor = cs_df[cs_df['LFSTAT'] == 3]['WTSURVY'].sum()
weight_labor_force = weight_employed + weight_unemployed

employment_rate = (weight_employed / weight_labor_force) * 100
unemployment_rate = (weight_unemployed / weight_labor_force) * 100
labor_force_participation_rate = (weight_labor_force / (weight_labor_force + weight_not_in_labor)) * 100

# Save filtered data with human-readable column names and year
output_df = cs_df[['OBSNUM', 'N2BAMED', 'LFSTAT', 'WTSURVY']].copy()
output_df.columns = ['Record_ID', 'Major_Code', 'Labor_Force_Status', 'Survey_Weight']

output_df['Year'] = YEAR

# Map LFSTAT to text labels
status_map = {1: 'Employed', 2: 'Unemployed', 3: 'Not in labor force'}
output_df['Status_Label'] = output_df['Labor_Force_Status'].map(status_map)

output_df = output_df[['Year', 'Record_ID', 'Major_Code', 'Labor_Force_Status', 'Status_Label', 'Survey_Weight']]

output_df.to_csv(OUTPUT_FILE, index=False)

import altair as alt

df = pd.read_csv("AI_Global_Trends_Dataset.csv")

df["Percent"] = df["AI (Any Function) %"]

    df["Percent"].astype(str)
        .str.replace('%','', regex=False)
        .str.replace('N/A.*','', regex=True),
    errors='coerce'
)

df["Percent"] *= 100

alt.data_transformers.disable_max_rows()  # allow larger datasets


# The graph below is created via layering; pre-defining shared encodings here to avoid duplicationg the definitions
x_enc = alt.X("Year:N", title="Year", axis=alt.Axis(labelAngle=0, labelFontSize=16, titleFontSize=18))
y_enc = alt.Y("Percent:Q",
             title="AI Adoption (%)",
             scale=alt.Scale(domainMax=100),

aiChart = alt.Chart(df).mark_bar(size=50).encode(
    x=x_enc,
    y=y_enc,
)

    align='center',
    baseline='bottom',

).transform_calculate(
    # Append the '%' symbol to the label
    label_with_pct="format(datum.Percent, '.1f') + '%'"
).encode(
    x=x_enc,
    y=y_enc,

)

final_aiChart = (aiChart + ai_text_labels).properties(

alt.data_transformers.enable("vegafusion")

# -----------------------------
# 1. Load NSCG microdata 2015–2023
# -----------------------------
file_pattern = "cs_related_employment_*.csv"
files = sorted(glob.glob(file_pattern))

df_list = []

for f in files:
    # Prevent loading the 2025 summary CSV, as that is a different csv format and needs to be handled on its own.
    if "2025" not in f:
        print(f"Reading {f}...")
        df = pd.read_csv(f)
        df_list.append(df)

combined = pd.concat(df_list, ignore_index=True)

print(f"Total records: {len(combined)}")


# Calculate weighted unemployment by year

results = []

for year, group in combined.groupby("Year"):

    w_emp = group[group["Labor_Force_Status"] == 1]["Survey_Weight"].sum()
    w_unemp = group[group["Labor_Force_Status"] == 2]["Survey_Weight"].sum()

    w_labor = w_emp + w_unemp

    rate = (w_unemp / w_labor) * 100 if w_labor > 0 else None

    results.append({
        "Year": int(year),
        "Unemployment_Rate": rate
    })

nscg_summary = pd.DataFrame(results)

# -----------------------------
# 3. Load 2025 CSV
# -----------------------------
csv_2025 = pd.read_csv("cs_related_employment_2025.csv")

# Average ALL unemployment rates (values are proportions)
avg_2025 = csv_2025["Unemployment rates"].mean()

# Append 2025 result
nscg_summary = pd.concat([
    nscg_summary,
    pd.DataFrame([{
        "Year": 2025,
        "Unemployment_Rate": avg_2025
    }])
], ignore_index=True)

# Sort years so line draws correctly
nscg_summary = nscg_summary.sort_values("Year")

csChart = alt.Chart(nscg_summary).mark_bar(
    size=50  # Adjusted size for better bar look
).encode(
    x=alt.X("Year:O", title="Year", axis=alt.Axis(labelAngle=0, labelFontSize=16, titleFontSize=18)),
    y=alt.Y("Unemployment_Rate:Q",
            title="Unemployment Rate (%)",
            scale=alt.Scale(domainMax=7),
            axis=alt.Axis(
                format=".1f",            # Sets decimal precision
                labelExpr="datum.label + '%'",  # Adds the symbol
                labelFontSize=16, titleFontSize=18
            )),
).properties(
    title=alt.TitleParams("Unemployment Rate for Computer Science-Related Graduates (2017–2025)",fontSize=18),
    description='CS-related occupations remain steady until (with the exception of the COVID-19 Pandemic where we see a spike), and suddenly spike to 6% in 2025.',
    width=500, # Widened slightly to fit the years better
    height=00
)

text_labels = alt.Chart(nscg_summary).mark_text(
    align='center',
    baseline='bottom',
    dy=-10,
    fontSize=14,
    fontWeight='bold'
).transform_calculate(
    # Format the number and manually append the %
    label_with_pct="format(datum.Unemployment_Rate, '.1f') + '%'"
).encode(
    x=alt.X("Year:O"),
    y=alt.Y("Unemployment_Rate:Q"),
    text=alt.Text("label_with_pct:N")
)

# 3. Layer them together
final_csChart = (csChart + text_labels).properties(
    title=alt.TitleParams(
        "Unemployment Rate for Computer Science-Related Graduates (2017–2025)",
        fontSize=22,
        anchor='start',
        subtitle="Unemployment remains at around the 3-4% level from 2017-2019, then spikes in the 2020s, with large spikes to 4.9% in 2021 and 6.4% in 2025."
    )
)

final_csChart
